label: Get involved
description: Volunteer roles beside the volunteer form, the other ways to help, questions and the newsletter.

settings.text: Most shifts are two to four hours. Come once a month or every week.

settings.heading: Volunteering
settings.text: No experience needed. Pick a role, tell us when you are free, and Luc will write within a week.

settings.title: Pantry shifts
settings.body: Stock the shelves, weigh deliveries and help neighbours shop. Shifts run from 9:30 to 13:00 or 13:00 to 16:30, Monday to Saturday.

settings.title: Breakfast kitchen
settings.body: Cook and serve the community breakfast on Tuesday and Thursday, from 7:00 to 10:00. Food hygiene training is free and takes an afternoon.

settings.title: Delivery drivers
settings.body: Take grocery boxes to neighbours who can't get out, on Friday mornings. You need a licence; we have the van.

settings.title: Garden crew
settings.body: Weed, water and harvest the beds behind Mill Hall, April to October. Saturday mornings, gloves provided.

settings.title: Front desk
settings.body: Welcome people as they arrive, answer the phone and keep the kettle on. Weekday shifts of three hours.

settings.heading: Other ways to help
settings.text: Not free for a shift? There is more than one way in.

settings.title: Donate food
settings.text: Bring tins and dry goods to Mill Hall.

settings.title: Fundraise
settings.text: Run, bake or host a supper for us.

settings.title: Give money
settings.text: Once or monthly, through our giving page.

settings.title: How old do I need to be?
settings.body: Eighteen for kitchen and delivery shifts. From fourteen you can join the garden crew or a pantry shift with a parent or guardian.

settings.title: Do you need a background check?
settings.body: Only for delivery drivers and anyone working with the kids' lunch club. We arrange it and pay for it.

settings.title: Do I need experience?
settings.body: No. Every first shift is next to someone who has done it before, and the kitchen roles start with a free food hygiene course.

settings.title: Can our group volunteer together?
settings.body: Yes. Workplaces, schools and faith groups of up to eight join a pantry or garden shift. Write to us with a few dates.

settings.heading: Newsletter
settings.text: One email a month with what we cooked, who helped and what the pantry needs.
